# Review of FDS 6.2, Tank Pressure Control

I reviewed this from the text alone, without P&IDs, the cause-and-effect matrix, the tank design basis or the compressor datasheet. Setpoints I add are marked **[TBC]** and must be confirmed against the tank design basis and the HAZOP/LOPA.

## Defect list

| # | Clause | Severity | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 6.2.5 | **Critical** | The claim that low pressure is not a concern is wrong. A full-containment tank tolerates very little vacuum. Barometric rise, a stuck-open flare valve, compressor over-capacity at low BOG generation, or a controller or transmitter failure can all pull the tank down, and a vacuum relief at -5 mbarg then admits air to a hydrocarbon space. There is no low alarm, low-low trip, make-up gas or minimum-pressure protection. |
| 2 | 6.2.3 | **Critical** | The high-high trip stops the BOG compressors, which are the primary means of removing vapor. At 250 mbarg, 40 mbar below the PSV set pressure, this removes pressure relief capacity at the worst moment. "Protect them" is not a valid reason for a tank-pressure trip. Compressors are protected by their own suction, discharge, vibration and temperature trips. The tank HH should instead stop the sources of pressure: close the LNG receipt and ship vapor-return valves, and stop any heat or flash inputs. |
| 3 | 6.2.4 | **Critical** | The HMI can bypass a safety trip with no controls. A bypass needs a key-switch or equivalent access control, an authorization record, a time limit, an alarm, and compensating measures. A bypass must not be possible while the tank is in service without these. |
| 4 | 6.2.2 | High | PV-512 behavior is underspecified. It has no ramp or split-range behavior, no closing setpoint or hysteresis, and no fail-safe position. Fail-open risks depressurizing the tank. Fail-closed loses the flare path. No flare-availability permissive is given. The relief capacity case (rollover, flash during unloading, atmospheric pressure drop, compressor trip) is not stated. |
| 5 | 6.2.1 | High | Compressor capacity control is undefined: the method, minimum turndown, duty/standby philosophy, auto-start of the standby unit, and behavior on controller or transmitter failure are all missing. "Run continuously" (6.2.5) conflicts with turndown at low BOG rates. |
| 6 | 6.2.1–6.2.3 | High | Instrument independence is not stated. PIC-501, PIC-510 and the HH trip must use separate transmitters and nozzles. The HH is a safety function and needs a SIL-assessed, voted (e.g. 2oo3) transmitter set that is independent of the BPCS. |
| 7 | 6.2.6 | Medium | There is no design basis for the relief devices. Design pressure and design vacuum are not stated, nor are the sizing cases or the number of valves (typically n+1 with an interlocked changeover). The PSV discharge destination (atmosphere or flare) is not stated. The vacuum relief setting of -5 mbarg is meaningful only against the tank design vacuum, and the low-low trip must sit well above it. |
| 8 | 6.2.7 | Medium | Anti-surge is delegated to the vendor with no interface definition. The recycle path and its cooling, the interaction with PIC-501 (recycle can mask or fight the pressure loop), the trip hand-offs and signals are not specified. If the compressors are reciprocating or screw, anti-surge does not apply and the requirement should be minimum-flow or unloader control. |
| 9 | 6.2 (general) | Medium | There is no pressure ladder, so alarm levels are missing. There is no HI alarm between 120 and 220 mbarg, and no deadbands or reset values. Operating modes (holding, ship unloading, turndown, compressor trip) are not addressed. There is no failure handling for bad-quality signals. Tag naming is inconsistent (PIC-501 vs PIC-510 for the same variable). |
| 10 | 6.2.1 | Low | Pressure is given in mbarg with no tolerance or barometric compensation note. A setpoint and its range should be stated. |

## Corrected section

**6.2 Tank Pressure Control**

**6.2.1 Pressure ladder.** Tank pressure (mbarg) shall be managed against the following levels. Values marked [TBC] are to be confirmed against the tank design basis and the safety study.

| Level | Pressure | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Vacuum relief valves open | -5 | Mechanical, last line of defense |
| PSLL (SIS) | 20 [TBC] | Trip BOG compressors K-501A/B, close flare valve PV-512 |
| PAL | 50 [TBC] | Alarm |
| Make-up gas valve opens | 70 [TBC] | Admit make-up gas to the tank vapor header |
| Normal control setpoint | 120 | PIC-501 |
| PAH | 170 [TBC] | Alarm |
| Flare valve opens | 220 | PIC-510 |
| PSHH (SIS) | 250 | Close LNG receipt and ship vapor-return valves; compressors and flare remain in service |
| PSVs open | 290 | Mechanical |

**6.2.2 Normal control.** PIC-501, using PT-501, shall control the capacity of the duty BOG compressor (K-501A or K-501B) to hold 120 mbarg [method per compressor datasheet, e.g. VFD, suction throttling or unloading]. The control range and minimum turndown shall be [TBC]. At minimum turndown, excess capacity shall be handled by [recycle or unloading, TBC] and not by stopping the compressor. If the duty compressor trips, the standby compressor shall start automatically. On failure or bad quality of PT-501, PIC-501 shall hold its last output, raise an alarm, and transfer control to the PT-510 signal.

**6.2.3 Flare relief.** PIC-510, using its own transmitter PT-510 on a separate nozzle, shall open PV-512 to the flare when pressure exceeds 220 mbarg, with the valve position proportional to the pressure above setpoint. PV-512 shall close at 200 mbarg [TBC]. PV-512 shall fail [closed or open, TBC from the relief and vacuum studies]. PV-512 shall be sized for [the governing BOG case, TBC]. Flare-header availability shall be an alarmed permissive.

**6.2.4 High-high pressure protection.** At 250 mbarg, a SIL-rated function [target TBC by LOPA] using three independent transmitters voted 2oo3, separate from the BPCS, shall:
- close the LNG receipt isolation valves and the ship vapor-return valves;
- initiate an alarm and inhibit any start permissive that adds load to the tank.

The BOG compressors and the flare path shall remain in service, and this trip shall not stop them. Compressor protection shall be provided by the compressors' own trips (suction and discharge pressure, temperature, vibration) as defined in 6.2.7.

**6.2.5 Bypass.** Bypass of the PSHH or PSLL function shall be possible only through a key-operated override switch under the shift supervisor's authority, with a written permit. The bypass shall be time-limited [TBC], continuously alarmed on the HMI, and logged. Compensating measures shall be defined in the permit. The bypass shall not be available from the HMI alone.

**6.2.6 Low-pressure and vacuum protection.**
- Below 50 mbarg [TBC], PAL shall alarm.
- Below 70 mbarg [TBC], the make-up gas valve shall open to admit make-up gas (vaporized LNG or send-out gas) to the vapor header and restore pressure.
- At 20 mbarg [TBC], PSLL shall trip both compressors and close PV-512.
- The compressors shall be allowed to operate continuously only while PIC-501 is in control and these protections are healthy.
- The vacuum relief valves at -5 mbarg are the last line of defense only. Their set pressure shall be confirmed against the tank design vacuum.

**6.2.7 Relief devices.**
- The tank PSVs shall be set at 290 mbarg, not above the tank design pressure of [TBC].
- The PSVs shall be installed n+1 with an interlocked changeover, sized for the governing case (rollover, flash, loss of compressors and fire) [TBC]. The discharge destination shall be [TBC].
- The vacuum relief valves shall be set at -5 mbarg, sized for [the governing case, TBC].

**6.2.8 Compressor protection and anti-surge.** The vendor package shall provide compressor protection and anti-surge (or minimum-flow or unloader control, depending on compressor type). The interface shall define:
- the signals exchanged with the control system: run status, load, fault, and recycle valve position;
- recycle gas cooling;
- how recycle interacts with PIC-501, so that recycle does not mask or fight the pressure loop;
- which package trips are hardwired to the SIS.

## Points to confirm

- **The intent of the original 6.2.3.** If the author meant to protect the compressors from high suction pressure, that belongs in the vendor's mechanical limits. A tank-pressure trip is the wrong variable for it.
- **Fail positions and ladder values.** Both depend on a study I haven't seen. Please confirm them with the HAZOP/LOPA before issuing.
